lane: meta-evolution, recursive self-improvement, and automated discovery
method: Rebuilt from the cited version of each primary paper. Retained PDFs and five versioned arXiv PDFs were converted with pdftotext. Every edge was checked in citation context and against the seed bibliography. Context is the citing authors' characterization, not independent verification of the cited work's findings.

seeds.title: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation
seeds.access: arXiv PDF v3; selected introduction, related work, formulation, and bibliography inspected
seeds.inspection_source: /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2023-stop.pdf; pdftotext extraction /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2023-stop.txt; downloaded directly from https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.02304v3 after no retained copy was found
seeds.limitations: The model weights do not change, so the paper explicitly distinguishes STOP from full recursive self-improvement.

edges.title: Gödel Machines: Self-Referential Universal Problem Solvers Making Provably Optimal Self-Improvements
edges.context: The authors use the Gödel-machine line as the rigorous formal precedent, while stressing that STOP neither proves optimality nor changes its underlying language model.
edges.identity_basis: Schmidhuber (2003/2007) is named in the paragraph and resolved to the full bibliography entry.

edges.title: Promptbreeder: Self-Referential Self-Improvement via Prompt Evolution
edges.locator: §2, Language Models as Prompt Engineers; bibliography
edges.context: Promptbreeder is grouped with prompt optimizers and contrasted with STOP's recursively applicable code scaffold.
edges.identity_basis: Exact title and author-year appear in the bibliography and related-work paragraph.

edges.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
edges.context: Voyager is related work in which an LM optimizes programs available to an embodied agent, rather than the optimizer-code loop used by STOP.
edges.identity_basis: Exact title is in the bibliography and Wang et al. (2023) is cited in the paragraph.

seeds.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
seeds.access: retained arXiv PDF v2; selected introduction, framing, related work, and bibliography inspected
seeds.limitations: Meta Agent Search uses a fixed meta-agent and a small benchmark set; it is not a self-modifying system.

edges.title: Mathematical Discoveries from Program Search with Large Language Models
edges.context: FunSearch is the precedent for foundation-model code generation inside evolutionary search; ADAS transfers that idea to whole agent systems.
edges.identity_basis: FunSearch and Romera-Paredes et al. (2024) appear in the prose and bibliography.

edges.title: Promptbreeder: Self-Referential Self-Improvement via Prompt Evolution
edges.locator: §2 and §5, Existing Attempts to ADAS; bibliography
edges.context: Promptbreeder represents the narrower prompt-only search space contrasted with representing all agent components in code.
edges.identity_basis: Exact title appears in the bibliography and PromptBreeder is named in the framing.

edges.title: AutoFlow: Automated Workflow Generation for Large Language Model Agents
edges.context: AutoFlow is cited as a workflow optimizer with a specialized representation; ADAS claims a broader code-defined design space.
edges.identity_basis: Exact title and arXiv identifier occur in the bibliography; AutoFlow is named in related work.

seeds.title: AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation
seeds.access: arXiv PDF v4; selected introduction, method framing, baseline discussion, appendix, and bibliography inspected
seeds.inspection_source: /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2024-aflow.pdf; pdftotext extraction /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2024-aflow.txt; downloaded directly from https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.10762v4 after no retained copy was found
seeds.limitations: The search fixes the model, temperature, output format, and operator set; benchmark configurations differ across comparisons.

edges.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
edges.context: AFlow adopts ADAS's code representation and argues that MCTS searches it more efficiently than ADAS's linear heuristic; ADAS is also an experimental baseline.
edges.identity_basis: Hu et al. (2024) is repeatedly cited as ADAS and resolves to the exact title.

edges.title: AutoFlow: Automated Workflow Generation for Large Language Model Agents
edges.context: AutoFlow is cited among prior attempts to automate workflow generation before AFlow motivates its graph/code search space.
edges.identity_basis: Li et al. (2024b) is cited in the introduction and the exact title/arXiv ID appear in the bibliography.

edges.title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into State-of-the-Art Pipelines
edges.context: DSPy illustrates methods requiring a human-specified workflow before prompt optimization, motivating search over workflow structure.
edges.identity_basis: Khattab et al. (2024) is cited in the argument and the exact title appears in the bibliography.

seeds.title: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
seeds.access: retained arXiv PDF v3; selected introduction, related work, method framing, and bibliography inspected
seeds.limitations: The empirical loop is confined to coding-agent repositories and replaces formal proof with benchmark evidence.

edges.title: Gödel Machines: Fully Self-Referential Optimal Universal Self-Improvers
edges.context: The theoretical Gödel machine is the explicit starting point; DGM relaxes proof and accepts empirically benchmarked changes.
edges.identity_basis: Schmidhuber (2007) is cited throughout and resolves to the full bibliography entry.

edges.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
edges.context: ADAS is the fixed-meta-agent predecessor; DGM instead uses one system to solve tasks and modify its own implementation.
edges.identity_basis: ADAS/Hu et al. is named in the paragraph and exact title appears in the bibliography.

edges.title: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation
edges.context: STOP is cited as an FM self-improvement system using a meta-agent and meta-utility; DGM distinguishes its self-modifying open-ended archive.
edges.identity_basis: Zelikman et al. (2024b) is described in the paragraph and resolves to STOP.

edges.title: A Self-Improving Coding Agent
edges.context: The authors call SICA the most similar concurrent work and distinguish DGM by archive-based open-ended exploration.
edges.identity_basis: Robeyns et al. (2025) is explicitly characterized as concurrent and the exact title/arXiv ID appear in the bibliography.

seeds.title: Huxley-Gödel Machine: Human-Level Coding Agent Development by an Approximation of the Optimal Self-Improving Machine
seeds.access: retained arXiv PDF v3; selected introduction, formalization, related work, baseline discussion, and bibliography inspected
seeds.limitations: Its Gödel-machine analogy depends on explicit assumptions and an estimated clade-metaproductivity proxy.

edges.title: Gödel Machines: Self-Referential Universal Problem Solvers Making Provably Optimal Self-Improvements
edges.context: HGM specializes Gödel-machine acceptance to coding-agent development and substitutes estimated clade-metaproductivity for an inaccessible proof/oracle criterion.
edges.identity_basis: The paper analyzes the Gödel-machine setup and includes the exact Schmidhuber entry.

edges.title: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
edges.context: DGM is a principal baseline and a member of the tree-search class HGM formalizes; HGM replaces immediate benchmark guidance with long-run clade productivity.
edges.identity_basis: DGM is named in prose, figures, comparisons, and the bibliography.

edges.title: A Self-Improving Coding Agent
edges.context: SICA is the second main coding-agent baseline and is modeled as a greedy branch of the same search tree.
edges.identity_basis: SICA/Robeyns et al. is named repeatedly and the exact title appears in the bibliography.

seeds.title: AlphaEvolve: A Coding Agent for Scientific and Algorithmic Discovery
seeds.access: retained arXiv PDF v1; selected introduction, system description, related work, and bibliography inspected
seeds.limitations: The white paper covers machine-gradable problems and selected discoveries; the system was not released in the inspected version.

edges.title: Mathematical Discoveries from Program Search with Large Language Models
edges.context: AlphaEvolve is called a substantial enhancement of FunSearch, moving from short single functions to larger multi-file, multi-objective code evolution.
edges.identity_basis: FunSearch is named repeatedly and resolved to Romera-Paredes et al. in the bibliography.

edges.title: Discovering Faster Matrix Multiplication Algorithms with Reinforcement Learning
edges.context: AlphaTensor is the specialized matrix-multiplication predecessor; AlphaEvolve positions itself as a general-purpose method.
edges.identity_basis: The text names AlphaTensor and reference [26] resolves to the Nature paper.

seeds.title: Hyperagents
seeds.access: retained arXiv PDF v1; selected introduction, related work, method, baseline, and bibliography sections inspected
seeds.limitations: The system starts from human-written task and meta-agents, and compounding evidence is bounded to reported domains and budgets.

edges.title: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
edges.context: Hyperagents replaces DGM's fixed instruction-generation mechanism with a modifiable meta-agent; original and manually customized DGM are baselines.
edges.identity_basis: DGM is central throughout and resolves to the exact Zhang et al. entry.

edges.title: Gödel Machines: Self-Referential Universal Problem Solvers Making Provably Optimal Self-Improvements
edges.context: The Gödel machine is the formal historical example of provably beneficial self-rewriting, contrasted with empirical modifiable meta-agents.
edges.identity_basis: Schmidhuber (2003) is named in related work and the full title appears in the bibliography.

edges.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
edges.context: The fixed-meta-agent ablation is said to replicate ADAS in this setting, isolating improvement of the improvement process.
edges.identity_basis: ADAS/Hu et al. is explicitly attached to the ablation and resolved in the bibliography.

seeds.title: Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds
seeds.access: arXiv PDF v1; selected introduction, method, evaluation comparison, related work, and bibliography inspected; temporary copy only
seeds.inspection_source: /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2026-dream-rsi.pdf; pdftotext extraction /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2026-dream-rsi.txt; downloaded directly from https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.14858v1 after no retained copy was found
seeds.limitations: The replay world is built from completed discovery histories, so off-policy scores inherit their coverage and counterfactual limits.

edges.title: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
edges.locator: §1, agent self-improvement survey sentence; §6, Self-Evolving Agents
edges.context: DGM is cited as an example of agent self-improvement and harness evolution. Dream-RSI does not discuss it as a tested comparator or a direct exploration-controller predecessor.
edges.identity_basis: The citations Zhang et al. (2026b) in §1 and §6 resolve to the DGM bibliography entry.

edges.title: AlphaEvolve: A Coding Agent for Scientific and Algorithmic Discovery
edges.context: AlphaEvolve is a representative fixed discovery loop and a reported algorithm-discovery comparator.
edges.identity_basis: AlphaEvolve/Novikov et al. appears in the table, prose, and bibliography.

edges.title: EvoX: Meta-Evolution for Automated Discovery
edges.context: EvoX explicitly optimizes search strategy and is a comparator; Dream-RSI adds reusable off-policy replay from accumulated histories.
edges.identity_basis: EvoX/Liu et al. (2026a) appears in comparison, related work, and bibliography.

edges.title: MLEvolve: A Self-Evolving Framework for Automated Machine Learning Algorithm Discovery
edges.locator: §6, AI-Driven Scientific and Algorithmic Discovery; Memory, History, and Experience Reuse
edges.context: MLEvolve reuses cross-branch information for future search; Dream-RSI turns completed histories into replay environments for alternative controllers.
edges.identity_basis: MLEvolve/Du et al. (2026) is named in both subsections and resolved in the bibliography.

seeds.title: EvoX: Meta-Evolution for Automated Discovery
seeds.access: retained arXiv PDF v2; selected introduction, related work, method, evaluation, and bibliography inspected
seeds.limitations: Comparisons use fixed iteration budgets but heterogeneous implementations; AlphaEvolve values are imported rather than rerun.

edges.title: AlphaEvolve: A Coding Agent for Scientific and Algorithmic Discovery
edges.context: AlphaEvolve exemplifies a manually specified MAP-Elites search strategy and supplies published comparison results for mathematical tasks.
edges.identity_basis: Reference [22] resolves to AlphaEvolve and is cited in framing and evaluation.

edges.title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
edges.context: GEPA selects candidates along Pareto frontiers and is rerun as a baseline against EvoX's evolving search strategy.
edges.identity_basis: Reference [1] is the exact GEPA title and appears in related work and experiments.

edges.title: OpenEvolve: An Open-Source Evolutionary Coding Agent
edges.context: OpenEvolve uses static elite/diversity heuristics and is run as a baseline for EvoX's adaptive strategy.
edges.identity_basis: Reference [28] is the official repository citation and appears in related work and experiments.

seeds.title: MLEvolve: A Self-Evolving Framework for Automated Machine Learning Algorithm Discovery
seeds.access: arXiv PDF v1; selected introduction, related work, method, main comparison tables, and bibliography inspected; temporary copy only
seeds.inspection_source: /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2026-mlevolve.pdf; pdftotext extraction /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2026-mlevolve.txt; downloaded directly from https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.06473v1 after no retained copy was found
seeds.limitations: Self-evolution means experience/search adaptation within fixed machinery; comparisons involve heterogeneous systems and budgets.

edges.title: MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering
edges.context: MLE-bench supplies the 75-task substrate and human medal thresholds used for the main results.
edges.identity_basis: Reference [24] gives the exact title and the benchmark is named in methods and evaluation.

edges.title: MLAgentBench: Evaluating Language Agents on Machine Learning Experimentation
edges.context: MLAgentBench is an early benchmark/system in the lineage of coding agents for machine-learning experimentation.
edges.identity_basis: Reference [11] gives the exact title and arXiv identifier.

edges.title: AlphaEvolve: A Coding Agent for Scientific and Algorithmic Discovery
edges.context: AlphaEvolve supplies the mathematical task set and a reported baseline testing generalization beyond ML engineering.
edges.identity_basis: Reference [6] is AlphaEvolve and it is named in experiment text and table.

edges.title: OpenEvolve: An Open-Source Evolutionary Coding Agent
edges.context: OpenEvolve is a specialized algorithm-discovery baseline on the AlphaEvolve mathematical task suite.
edges.identity_basis: Reference [38] is the official repository citation and OpenEvolve is named in the comparison.

seeds.title: Escher-Loop: Mutual Evolution by Closed-Loop Self-Referential Optimization
seeds.access: arXiv PDF v2; selected introduction, method, related work, and bibliography inspected; temporary copy only
seeds.inspection_source: /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2026-escher-loop.pdf; pdftotext extraction /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2026-escher-loop.txt; downloaded directly from https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.23472v2 after no retained copy was found
seeds.limitations: The implementation starts from OpenEvolve and reports bounded-domain optimization; it does not establish unbounded self-improvement.

edges.title: OpenEvolve: An Open-Source Evolutionary Coding Agent
edges.context: The system is instantiated on OpenEvolve, then a population of optimizer programs replaces its fixed search heuristic.
edges.identity_basis: OpenEvolve/Sharma (2025) is named in implementation and bibliography.

edges.title: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation
edges.context: STOP is among empirical LLM systems that remove the target/meta-agent boundary by rewriting their own code or scaffold.
edges.identity_basis: STOP/Zelikman et al. is named in the paragraph and exact bibliography entry.

edges.title: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
edges.context: DGM replaces greedy updates with a tree of historical variants; Escher-Loop co-evolves optimizer populations with solutions.
edges.identity_basis: DGM/Zhang et al. appears in the paragraph and exact bibliography entry.

seeds.title: The Economics of Recursive Self-Improvement
seeds.access: retained arXiv PDF v1; selected introduction, model framing, literature positioning, calibration discussion, and bibliography inspected
seeds.limitations: This is theoretical modeling and calibration; conclusions depend on poorly measured elasticities and bottlenecks rather than an implemented recursive agent.

edges.title: When Does Automating AI Research Produce Explosive Growth? Feedback Loops in Innovation Networks
edges.context: The network models build on Davidson et al.'s theory of innovation networks and economic feedback loops, specialized here to recursive AI improvement and measurement.
edges.identity_basis: Davidson et al. (2026) is repeatedly cited and the exact NBER title appears in the bibliography.

edges.title: What a Compute-Centric Framework Says About Takeoff Speeds
edges.context: Davidson's compute-centric framework is credited as an early formal model of AI takeoff dynamics broadened here with multiple inputs and bottlenecks.
edges.identity_basis: Davidson (2023) is named in the paragraph and exact report title appears in the bibliography.

edges.title: Artificial Intelligence, Automation, and Work
edges.context: Aghion et al. are identified as foundational economics work on conditions for AI automation to generate accelerating or explosive growth.
edges.identity_basis: Aghion et al. (2017) is named in the paragraph and resolved to the bibliography.

seeds.title: A Self-Improving Coding Agent
seeds.access: arXiv PDF v2; selected introduction, related work, method, Algorithm 1, limitations, and bibliography inspected; temporary copy only
seeds.inspection_source: /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2025-sica-v2.pdf; pdftotext extraction /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2025-sica-v2.txt; downloaded directly from https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.15228v2 after no retained copy was found
seeds.limitations: The archive informs proposals, but each iteration expands from the current best-scoring agent; proposal anchoring, path dependence, static benchmarks, and time/cost-sensitive utility constrain the evidence.

edges.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
edges.context: SICA adopts ADAS's archive-and-evaluate loop but makes the best archived agent the next meta-agent, whereas ADAS keeps a fixed meta-agent and archives only target agents.
edges.identity_basis: ADAS/Hu et al. [16] is named in the mechanism comparison and resolves to the exact bibliography title.

edges.title: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP): Recursively Self-Improving Code Generation
edges.context: STOP is cited as recursively improving optimizer code on algorithmic tasks; SICA distinguishes its general coding-agent scaffold and self-editing software-engineering setting.
edges.identity_basis: Zelikman et al. [47] is described in §2 and resolves to the exact STOP title in the bibliography.

edges.title: Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement
edges.context: Gödel Agent is cited as a self-referential predecessor with specialized tools and non-general coding evaluations, against which SICA positions its editable general coding scaffold.
edges.identity_basis: Gödel Agent/Yin et al. [44] is named and characterized in §2 and resolved in the bibliography.

seeds.title: Gödel Machines: Self-Referential Universal Problem Solvers Making Provably Optimal Self-Improvements
seeds.access: arXiv PDF v5; abstract, proof-search mechanism, global-optimality theorem, related-work comparison, and bibliography inspected; temporary copy only
seeds.inspection_source: /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2003-goedel-machine-arxiv.pdf; pdftotext extraction /tmp/meta-citation-audit.7mmz3G/2003-goedel-machine-arxiv.txt; downloaded directly from https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/0309048
seeds.limitations: The guarantee is conditional on the encoded axioms, utility, resources, and proof-search process; useful target theorems may be difficult or impossible to prove in time.

edges.title: Towards a Universal Theory of Artificial Intelligence Based on Algorithmic Probability and Sequential Decisions
edges.context: Hutter's AIXI lineage supplies a universal expected-reward problem solver whose meta-algorithm remains hardwired; the Gödel machine makes its proof searcher and all other software rewritable.
edges.identity_basis: Hutter [16] is discussed by name in §6.4 and resolved to the exact bibliography title.

edges.title: The Fastest and Shortest Algorithm for All Well-Defined Problems
edges.context: HSEARCH is a non-self-referential proof-search predecessor with asymptotic optimality; the paper contrasts it with a proof searcher that may rewrite itself and improve large constants.
edges.identity_basis: Hutter [17] is explicitly compared in §6.4 and the exact title appears in the bibliography.

edges.title: Reinforcement Learning with Self-Modifying Policies
edges.context: Earlier self-modifying-policy work uses empirical success-history backtracking; the Gödel machine is distinguished by proof-gated changes under its formal utility criterion.
edges.identity_basis: Schmidhuber, Zhao, and Schraudolph [53] is discussed in item 5 and resolved to the exact bibliography title.

recommendations.detail: Remove STOP→DGM, STOP→Self-Adapting Language Models, ADAS→AFlow, AFlow→GEPA, AlphaEvolve→DGM, MLEvolve→EvoX, and Economics of RSI→AlphaEvolve/DGM. None occurs in the inspected seed text. Retain Dream-RSI→DGM only as a generic foundation edge at §1/§6, not as the previously claimed direct predecessor at §6.2.
Use register keys hyperagents, harness-evolution-evaluation, evoharnessbench, wikiskill, library-drift, and metarsi; year-prefixed worker variants are invalid.

Retain Gödel Machines, A Self-Improving Coding Agent, FunSearch, OpenEvolve, MLE-bench, MLAgentBench, and Davidson et al.'s innovation-network model in aggregation even without dedicated notes; each is a direct foundation, implementation, or tested baseline.

limits: Fourteen seeds audited: seven retained PDFs and seven versioned arXiv PDFs downloaded temporarily (STOP v3, AFlow v4, Dream-RSI v1, MLEvolve v1, Escher-Loop v2, SICA v2, Gödel Machines v5). Cited identities were checked against seed bibliographies and canonical metadata. Most cited works without session notes were not substantively re-read, so their findings remain unverified beyond the citing authors' characterization.
